justification: The garden does not need tending every week, only watching. Mr. Pickens bloomed for twenty points the last time I trusted him over the louder name on my bench, and I see no sign yet that the lesson has expired, so he keeps his place in the flex ahead of a Mr. Wilson who is owed patience, not a start, over a difference of less than a point that the numbers cannot truly explain to me. Olave, Washington, and Warren all did quiet, honest work last week, and quiet, honest work is rewarded with another week of trust, not a bench. Denver's defense found a pick-six and thirteen points without my asking twice, which is precisely why I will not ask it to do anything differently now. Daniels remains the obvious throne, and I have learned that the obvious choice is sometimes simply correct. As for the Golden Child across the table this week — he has already told the room he is the headline. I find a man who announces his own ending rarely gets to choose it.
